2. Heard Ms. Anjali Patil, learned counsel for the  Applicant, Mr. Shrikant H. Yadav, learned APP for the State and  Ms. Prachi Tatke, learned counsel for the Respondent No.2.
 3.
The prosecution case is that the victim in this case was  about 17 years of age.
The Applicant was following her since she  was studying in 9th standard.
He had proposed marriage to her.
But she had refused.
She had not told about that to anybody out  of fear.
She knew that the Applicant was already married.
In the  year 2015 on one occasion her parents were sleeping outside  their house.
She was in the house.
In that night, the Applicant  came to her house and committed sexual intercourse.
This was  repeated on two more occasions.
According to her, she did not  tell about it to anybody out of fear.
She became pregnant.

Thereafter, the Doctor lodged complaint with  the police.
The investigation was carried out and the Applicant  faced the trial.
4. Learned counsel for the Applicant submitted that it was  a clear case of consensual relationship.
The Applicant was  married to the victim.
She was aware that the Applicant was  earlier married.
Learned counsel for the Applicant submitted  that the Applicant was a divorcee and after his divorce he  married the victim.
She relied on the evidence of D.W.1 Rajesh  Gore, who had deposed about the marriage between the victim  and the Applicant.
She further submitted that ossification test  shows that the victim was between 17 and 19 years of age.
Therefore, according to her there was strong possibility that the  victim was above 18 years of age.
No case u/s 376 or u/s 6 of  POCSO is made out.
She further submitted that the school  record was produced in the form of a photocopy.
The original  was not produced and therefore there was doubt about her age  as alleged by the prosecution.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the Respondent No.2 and learned  APP opposed these submissions.
According to them, there is  sufficient material to show that the victim was a minor and in  any case, the offence was committed against her wish and  therefore, the conviction was properly recorded.
6. I have considered these submissions.
As far as the  ossification test is concerned it is not conclusive piece of  evidence in the present case.
Learned Counsel for the  Respondents submitted that the ossification test was conducted  after one year.
In any case, there is a period of two years which  is mentioned as approximate period between 17 and 19 years
as  far as the victim's age is concerned.
The evidence of D.W.1  Rajesh Gore shows that he was proprietor of Mangal Karyalay  where the marriage between the Applicant and the victim took  place.
At that time, he had verified the documents of the victim  as well as of the Applicant.

The documents were in the nature of  school certificate and Aadhar card and the victim's age was  mentioned as 19 years.
 7.

Thus, considering all these submissions, there appears ::: Uploaded on - 15/06/2024 ::: Downloaded on - 24/06/2024 08:14:50 ::
 5/5 15-IA-1066-23-IN-APEAL-955-22.odt  to be some serious doubt about the age of the victim and  whether she was a minor at the time of incident.
Apart from  that, the victim's evidence shows that there is strong possibility  that it was a consensual relationship.

It is difficult to accept the Santosh Balu Dongare vs State Of Maharashtra And Anr on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/43959221/
4  prosecution story that this incident took place on number of  occasions against her will, particularly when, her parents were  in the vicinity.

sentences.text: The Applicant was on bail during trial and there  are no allegations that he had misused the liberty.
Considering  all these aspects, the Applicant deserves to be released on bail  during pendency of his Appeal.

8 . Hence, the following order :
 ORDER (i) During pendency and final disposal of the Criminal Appeal No.955 of 2022, the Applicant is directed to be released on bail on his furnishing P.R. Bond in the sum of Rs.30,000/- (Rupees Thirty Thousand Only), with one or two sureties in the like amount.
(ii) The application is disposed of.
